extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A realworld dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two omnidirectional cameras in a vertical arrangement, which prevents occlusion, and paired with a synchronized LiDAR sensor to provide high-quality depth measurements.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The rig features two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup with a 19.1 cm baseline, capturing equirectangular images at 30 fps, paired with a Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor with a vertical field of view of 42.4°, operating at 10 fps, and mounted 45.0 cm below the bottom camera.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Our approach interpolates depth on spherical grid points by using temporally aggregated point clouds and applies a filtering process to exclude points with high uncertainty or lacking nearby measurements, ensuring minimal error before mapping the remaining points.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: After cropping unnecessary regions (sky, ground), the resulting dataset comprises 39,553 paired images with their corresponding depth and disparity maps, at a resolution of 1920×512 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset includes accurate depth and disparity labels by projecting 3D point clouds onto equirectangular images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: This approach is limited for fast-moving objects like cars.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: HELVIPAD serves as a foundational resource for developing and benchmarking omnidirectional depth estimation models capable of navigating in human environments.
